input.quote: 11.1 Immediately on termination Vendor shall discontinue all assistance and permanently delete Customer Data without offering an export or migration support.
input.rationale: Sections 11.2 and 11.3 already deliver the data-return and certified-deletion limbs of the preferred position (return within 30 days of request in a commonly used, machine-readable format; certified deletion only after Customer confirms successful return). However, Section 11.1 sits squarely in walk-away territory: it requires immediate cessation of all assistance and permanent deletion of Customer Data on termination with no export or migration support, and it directly contradicts 11.2/11.3. There is no transition-assistance period anywhere in the agreement, so the clause fails even the 90-day fallback. We replaced 11.1 with up to six months of transition assistance at Vendor's then-current rates and subordinated deletion to Sections 11.2 and 11.3, resolving the internal inconsistency with the smallest possible edit; 90 days remains an acceptable fallback.

ops.oldText: Immediately on termination Vendor shall discontinue all assistance and permanently delete Customer Data without offering an export or migration support.
ops.newText: On expiry or termination of this Agreement or any Order Form for any reason, Vendor shall, at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six months at Vendor's then-current rates, including reasonable export and migration support. Vendor shall not delete Customer Data except in accordance with Sections 11.2 and 11.3.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We replaced the immediate cut-off and deletion of Customer Data with up to six months of transition assistance at your then-current rates, so exit is orderly and consistent with Sections 11.2 and 11.3. If six months is too long, we can accept 90 days.
proposal.summary: Replace immediate-deletion clause with 6-month transition assistance and align deletion with 11.2/11.3.
